To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the star glyph and the radial color encoding are not as effective as expected, that radial glyph layouts are the best choice when it comes to detecting specific points in a time series, and that metaphoric data glyphs can provide additional support in visualizing temporal and multi-dimensional information.

(1) star glyphs are not superior to whisker glyphs and radial color encoding layouts, (2) radial glyph layouts making the use of visual variables other than position outperform alternative layouts in detecting specific points, and (3) metaphoric data glyphs like the clock glyph and the leaf glyph can be successfully used in practice.
(1) The design of a data glyph is influenced by the data to encode, the task the analyst is performing, and the visual variables used to encode the information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of data glyphs, i.e. visual representations of data that are intended to convey information to the human observer, which are used in the context of temporal and multi-dimensional datasets.
providing guidance for researchers and practitioners to create and select data glyphs for specific tasks and data domains.
the design of data glyphs for temporal data and multi-dimensional data in information visualization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design considerations and evaluation presented in this thesis provide a valuable basis for the design and selection of glyphs for temporal and multidimensional data.
the results of the conducted studies and experiments are not conclusive, but rather indicate that the selection of a specific data glyph design depends on the task and the data to be represented.
data glyph designs should be tailored towards a specific data type, domain, and task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide guidance in designing and selecting data glyphs for temporal data and multi-dimensional data, based on a systematic literature review, quantitative experiments, and new metaphoric glyph designs.
we have contributed to the research field by providing a comprehensive review and analysis of data glyphs in the context of multi-dimensional and temporal data.

we have provided researchers and practitioners with an extended catalog of design considerations, which can be used for selecting and creating data glyphs for temporal data and multi-dimensional data in general.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is still a need for additional support for researchers and practitioners to design data glyphs.
the visual design of data glyphs is not trivial. It requires an understanding of the data, the task and the user.
data glyphs are a powerful tool for visualizing temporal data, but also for representing data with a high dimensionality.
